description: WCH Jiangsu Qin Heng CH32V003J4M6 — 32-bit RISC-V (RV32EC) MCU, 48 MHz, 16 KB flash, 2 KB SRAM, SOP-8 package. The cheapest microcontroller in the world (~$0.10) with an actual modern ISA. Six GPIOs (one shared with single-wire-debug PD1), one UART, one I²C, one SPI, one 8-channel 10-bit ADC, several 16-bit timers. The tiny-MCU complement to ESP32-S3 for cost-sensitive / space-constrained / no-wireless designs.
name: ch32v003j4m6
watch_out_for: Programming uses WCH's proprietary single-wire-debug (SWIO) on PD1 (pin 5) — needs a WCH-LinkE or compatible programmer (~$5). Arduino IDE supports the chip via the wch_riscv core; PlatformIO via the ch32v platform. Internal RC oscillator (~24 MHz scaled to 48 MHz via internal PLL) is ±2-5% — fine for UART up to 115200 baud, but for precise timing (USB, audio) you need an external crystal, which the SOP-8 doesn't pin out — for crystal access switch to TSSOP-20 (CH32V003F4P6). Reset (PD7) is shared with a GPIO — if you tie PD7 low at boot you get continuous resets. 3.3 V supply only (3.0-5.0 V absolute max); not 5 V tolerant on I/O. Toolchain: GCC for RISC-V (riscv-none-elf-gcc), available pre-built from WCH or Nuclei Studio.
